Enhancing anomaly detection and 
prevention in Internet of Things 
(IoT) using deep neural networks 
and blockchain based cyber 
security
Sathyabama A R & Jeevaa Katiravan
The rapid adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has significantly increased cybersecurity 
risks, making them vulnerable to anomalies, attacks, and unauthorized access. Traditional security 
mechanisms struggle to handle the massive data flow, real-time processing requirements, and 
evolving cyber threats in IoT networks. This paper presents an integrated approach using Deep Neural 
Networks and Blockchain technology (DNNs-BCT) to enhance anomaly detection and prevention 
in IoT environments. Our proposed framework employs DNNs for intelligent anomaly detection, 
leveraging multi-layer feature extraction and adaptive learning mechanisms. The DNN model is 
trained on IoT traffic datasets to classify network behavior as normal or anomalous, effectively 
detecting threats such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, malware injections, and 
insider threats. Unlike traditional rule-based intrusion detection systems (IDS), the DNN continuously 
learns and adapts to new attack patterns, improving detection accuracy and false-positive reduction. 
This study integrates Blockchain technology into the IoT ecosystem to ensure data integrity, 
transparency, and decentralized security. Each IoT device logs its activity onto a private blockchain 
network, preventing data tampering, unauthorized access, and single points of failure. The blockchain 
employs smart contracts for automated threat response, instantly mitigating malicious activity 
without human intervention. This distributed ledger approach enhances trust, authentication, and 
secure communication across IoT devices. The synergy between DNN-based anomaly detection and 
Blockchain-based security provides a robust, scalable, and adaptive solution for real-time cybersecurity 
threats in IoT networks. With a low false-positive rate of 15.42% and a strong detection accuracy of 
99.18%, the proposed model successfully identifies malicious activity, including malware injections 
and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) assaults. Blockchain technology replaces single points of 
failure and forbids illegal changes by providing data integrity, openness, and decentralizing powers. 
Furthermore, smart contracts allow autonomous, real-time attack responses, enhancing reaction time 
efficiency (95.25%) and general system scalability (94.96%).
Keywords IoT security, Deep neural networks, Blockchain, Anomaly detection, Cybersecurity, Smart 
contracts, Distributed ledger, Threat prevention, Intrusion detection, Federated learning
The Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed several industries by allowing connected smart objects to 
communicate, operate autonomously, and enhance efficiency in operations 1. From home automation and 
connected vehicles to industrial automation, health monitoring, and intelligent cities, IoT uses range from IoT 
networks’ decentralized nature, resource-limited devices, and the vast amount of real-time data they generate, 
thus rendering them highly susceptible to cybersecurity issues despite their advantages 2. Frequently unable to 
adequately cope with these changing risks are legacy security solutions such as centralized security architectures 
and rule-based intrusion detection systems (IDS)3. As IoT environments grow, advanced cyberattacks necessitate 
new-age security solutions to protect them4. Anomaly detection ranks among the most critical concerns in the 
security of IoT, i.e., recognizing departures from expected network behavior indicative of likely intrusions 5. In

IoT networks, typical attacks include data breaches, malware injections, DDoS attacks, and insider threats 6. 
Traditional IDS are based on accepted rules and signature-based approaches, which leads to significant false-
positive rates and the inability to detect emerging attack trends 7. Especially DNNs and artificial intelligence 
(AI)-based technologies have received much attention to end these constraints since they can learn intricate 
patterns, update from evolving threats, and achieve very high detection accuracy8.
Using multi-layer feature extraction, adaptive learning methods, and high computing capabilities, DNNs can 
evaluate large volumes of IoT network data9. Training on benchmark IoT datasets enables DNNs to characterize 
network activity as normal or aberrant, enabling little human intervention in risk detection. DNN-based models 
are more resistant to unknown cyber threats and zero-day attacks than traditional security systems, as they always 
improve by learning from new attack events10.While artificial intelligence aids cybersecurity anomaly detection, 
preserving data quality and confidence in IoT systems remains challenging11. Systems with centralized security 
abound in single points of failure, unauthorized data modifications, and privacy intrusions. One distributed 
tamper-proof solution for these issues is blockchain technology. Blockchain technology with IoT security, data 
integrity, openness, and trust will greatly improve these features12. Every IoT device logs activities on a private 
blockchain network, ensuring secure communication and preventing unlawful access. Fundamental blockchain 
components, such as smart contracts, enable automatic response to threats, thus minimizing negative behavior 
in realtime without human intervention13.
A new approach to enhance anomaly detection and cybersecurity in IoT systems is DNN with Blockchain 
technology (DNNs-BCT). Blockchain supports safe data management and distribution; DNNs provide 
remarkable accuracy in intelligent threat detection14. This combination generates a scalable, adaptable, tamper-
proof security solution to protect IoT devices from cyberattacks.Combining blockchain-based security measures 
with artificial intelligence-driven anomaly detection, this article provides a DNNs-BCT architecture to solve 
IoT cybersecurity problems 15. The solution that performs better in threat detection accuracy, false-positive 
minimization, and real-time reaction efficiency than standard IDS systems is evaluated using benchmark IoT 
data16. Future research will focus on developing lightweight DNN architectures for IoT devices with limited 
resources and investigating federated learning approaches to facilitate scalability and decentralization 17. This 
paper provides the route for autonomous, self-learning, tamper-proof security solutions in IoT networks 
employing artificial intelligence connected with blockchain, as shown in Table 1.
Scientific problem in existing evaluation
A more intelligent, scalable, and tamper-proof evaluation framework is urgently needed to address the 
shortcomings of current IoT anomaly detection and cybersecurity evaluation methods, such as high false 
positive rates, limited adaptability to evolving cyber threats, and vulnerability to adversarial attacks. Centralized 
security architectures create single points of failure, making them vulnerable to breaches and tampering. 
Existing evaluation models often lack transparency and verifiability, making it difficult to ensure the integrity 
and reliability of verified threats.
Combining deep learning (DL) with optimized feature selection techniques (PCA, RFE, and Mutual 
Information), DNNs-BCT improves classification accuracy and reduces false positives. At the same time, 
traditional machine learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) like SVM, k-NN, and Random Forest 
struggle with high-dimensional IoT traffic and evolving attack patterns. By utilizing a lightweight permissioned 
blockchain (such as Hyperledger Fabric or a custom PoA/DAG model), DNNs-BCT ensures faster transaction 
Motivation Problem statement
IoT devices’ exponential development has raised serious security issues as they are distributed, have limited processing capabilities, and are prone to 
cyberattacks. Conventional security solutions fail to provide real-time anomaly detection and prevention, increasing data breaches, malware attacks, 
and unauthorized access risks. Employing intelligent anomaly detection and distributed tamper-proof protection, this paper integrates Blockchain 
technology with DNN to tackle these difficulties, thereby increasing IoT security.

blockchain-based security solutions that depend on Ethereum or Bitcoin, which have high computational costs, 
energy consumption, and latency. In addition, current AI models may be manipulated by adversaries, and even 
small changes can dupe detection systems. DNNs-BCT integrates blockchain-authenticated anomaly logs to 
reduce this risk, prevent data manipulation, and make models more resilient. In addition, DNNs-BCT uses edge 
computing to preprocess data before DNN inference and blockchain logging, greatly reducing bandwidth load 
and allowing for real-time anomaly detection. This is in contrast to many AI-based models, which have high 
computational resource requirements and are thus unsuitable for IoT deployment. A more realistic and effective 
solution for real-world IoT cybersecurity, DNNs-BCT surpasses previous accuracy, efficiency, and security 
models by integrating DL adaptive detection capabilities with a scalable, low-overhead blockchain.
The remaining section of this paper is structured as follows: In section " Related work", the related work 
of Blockchain-Based Cybersecurity is studied. In section " Proposed method ", the proposed methodology of

analyzed. Finally, in section "Conclusion", the paper concludes with future work.
Related work
Several anomaly detection methods under investigation might help to secure IoMT-Blockchain and IoHT 
systems. Emphasizing real-time detection, data security, and simplicity reduction, these comprise multi-
model autoencoders, DNN, and blockchain integrations. These techniques seek to improve system integrity via 
IoT and blockchain networks using enhanced anomaly detection, assuring healthcare data’s safe delivery.For 
aberrant traffic identification in an IoMT-Blockchain context, the suggested technique presents a multi-model 
autoencoder-based feature-extracting algorithm18. It uses multi-model autoencoders to extract fusion features 
and aggregate traffic characteristics to lower complexity. Applying residual learning for anomaly detection and 
classification, a multi-feature sequence anomaly detection system is also meant to capture low-level fusion and 
high-level temporal information.
Artificial intelligence models are integrated with IPFS blockchain technology in the research to secure and 
distribute healthcare IoT data. The paper evaluates the performance of artificial intelligence techniques such 
as Support Vector Machines (SVM) in predicting outcomes with the TON_IoT, Edge_IIoT, and UNSW-NB15 
datasets19. The models show excellent accuracy, with the TON_IoT dataset achieving 100%, Edge_IIoT at 98%, 
and UNSW-NB15 at 89%. Blockchain is applied for enhanced data security, ensuring secure medical data 
distribution.The suggested method utilizes four DNN hidden layers for attack and standard data classification 
in cyber-physical systems20. Blocks with headers and secure data delivery for safe transportation are constructed 
and used to make the Ethereum blockchain work. Two datasets, namely NSL-KDD15 and CIDDS_001, have 
been utilized in this approach compared to current models such as RNN, DBN, and DNN and have found 
improved performance in identifying anomalies.
This paper extensively overviews anomaly detection model integration in blockchain technologies. It addresses 
how anomaly detection models across several blockchain layers21 can improve blockchain security, finds critical 
assessment criteria and prerequisites for creating effective models, and strengthens blockchain security. The 
paper discusses important problems and recommendations for further studies to address them.By processing 
data near IoT nodes, the suggested method employs edge-based computing to lower latency and bandwidth 
needs22. It uses smart contracts to stop insider assaults and preserve data integrity, then adds blockchain for safe 
anomaly discovery and repair. The system also reduces single points of failure, therefore increasing availability. 
Evaluating IoT datasets reveals the efficient method to solve these problems, thus guaranteeing data integrity 
and availability.
Focusing on the underlying network rather than ledger data, this paper provides a security method using 
blockchain network traffic statistics to identify hostile occurrences. Real-time multi-dimensional traffic data 
is captured by it using a data collecting engine 23). The anomaly detection engine efficiently finds hitherto 
unrecorded trends based on semi-supervised learning and an AutoEncoder (AE) profiling-based method. 
With real-time detection capabilities that require less than 1.4 ms for each occurrence, experimental data reveal 
that the mechanism’s performance is equivalent to supervised learning approaches.This article introduces 
blockchain technology and discusses its features, difficulties, and many cyberattacks, including Sybil attacks, 
selfish mining, double spending, and 51% assaults. Then, to address these cyber-attacks, deep anomaly detection 
(DL-based) systems are evaluated to underline many strategies, including discriminative, generative, and hybrid 
learning24. Furthermore, the study discusses techniques for improving the blockchain system’s security and real-
time anomaly detection powers.This work suggests an enhanced anomaly detection system to improve cloud 
security25 by combining QoS-aware sidechains, DL models (RNNs and CNNs), and multimodal feature analysis. 
Using improved prediction accuracy and system performance (precision, recall, AUC, energy consumption, and 
throughput), the system analyses system logs to discover odd assaults-related behaviors, optimizing blockchain-
based cloud installations. Blockchain guarantees system log integrity; DL offers exact anomaly detection in real-
time environments.
Asrin Vakili et al.27 suggested the grey wolf optimization algorithm and MapReduce framework for a new 
service composition method in the cloud-based IoT environment. The results of the simulation show that the 
proposed method improves upon the previous one in terms of availability, cost, reaction time, and energy 
savings. On average, the proposed method improves upon three baseline algorithms by cutting energy savings 
by 40%, reaction time by 14%, availability by 11%, and cost by 24%.
Zahra Amiri et al. 28 proposed DL applications in IoT-based bio- and medical informatics. The effective 
qualities, such as the basic concept, advantages, downsides, methodologies, simulation environment, and 
datasets, were examined using a comprehensive literature review. Following that, there was an emphasis on 
state-of-the-art research on DL methods and their applications concerning bioinformatics issues. Furthermore,

the blockchain-based DL method in IoD settings. According to the results, the proposed model is a great choice

performance. The results demonstrate that these assessment techniques have the potential to significantly 
improve fault handling, decrease damage risk, and enable WSN developers to make informed decisions.

Proposed method
Modern networks’ security needs a mix of sophisticated technology. This paper investigates blockchain-based 
threat response, DNN for network anomaly detection, and AI-powered anomaly detection combined with 
blockchain for IoT security. It also addresses DL models-based maritime and IoT traffic anomaly detection. 
These methodologies improve cybersecurity by guaranteeing data integrity, openness, and threat reduction.
Existing IoT anomaly detection techniques often suffer from elevated false alarm rates, ineffective real-time 
threat categorization, and susceptibility to adversarial attacks. Moreover, centralized security frameworks render 
IoT networks vulnerable to single points of failure, where corrupted nodes might threaten the integrity of the 
whole system. Current blockchain-based security models, while they guarantee data integrity, often experience 
significant computational overhead and delay, restricting their practical use in resource-limited IoT settings. The 
proposed DNN and Blockchain Technology (DNNs-BCT) framework mitigates these limitations by establishing 
a novel DL and blockchain integration wherein a lightweight DNN architecture enhances anomaly detection, 
and a smart contract-based blockchain mechanism guarantees secure, immutable logging and automated 
remediation. This approach improves threat intelligence, scalability, and real-time flexibility while decreasing 
computing complexity, representing a notable breakthrough over traditional methods.

This paper covers anomaly detection led by AI in IoT networks, blockchain transactions, and marine security. 
Blockchain guarantees openness and confidence; DL models extract characteristics, categorize abnormalities, 
and trigger automatic reactions. These methods enhance danger identification and prevention, from monitoring 
vessel movements to protecting IoT communications. Integrating blockchain and AI strengthens cybersecurity, 
lowering risks and maintaining system integrity.
Misclassification of threats and decreased anomaly detection accuracy may occur due to adversarial assaults, 
in which small changes in input data trick DL networks. Implementing adversarial training, gradient masking, 
and detection techniques might strengthen the resistance of the DNN model against such assaults. Furthermore, 
weaknesses in smart contracts, Sybil attacks, and 51% assaults may still penetrate blockchain-based security 
procedures and jeopardize the network’ s consensus and integrity. Formal smart contract verification, reputation-
based consensus methods, and lightweight cryptographic algorithms to guarantee blockchain security without 
excessive computational complexity should be included in the framework to avoid these dangers.
Result and discussion
Among the key cybersecurity issues brought about by the fast spread of IoT devices are unauthorized access, 
malware assaults, and data breaches. Changing attack strategies and real-time threats test conventional security 
solutions. This paper suggests blockchain-based architecture and integrated DNN to ensure data integrity, 
enhance anomaly detection, and offer IoT networks autonomous, distributed threat-mitigating properties.
Dataset description
The global digital security control system market is expected to grow from USD 15 billion in 2023 to USD 34 
billion by 2032, with a CAGR of 9.5%. Three key drivers behind growth are rising cyberthreats, increasing IoT 
usage, and tight legal regulations. Among the technical breakthroughs are artificial intelligence, blockchain, 
and open security possibilities for machine learning26. North America dominates the sector, even though quick 
digitalization and rising cyberattacks will most likely force Asia Pacific to have the highest growth.CICIDS2017 
records traffic from actual assaults such as DDoS, brute force, and penetration, while NSL-KDD gives organized 
data about attacks but has limitations because of old patterns. Ideal for real-time anomaly detection, UNSW-
NB15 and Bot-IoT provide current IoT-specific threats, including spoofing, injection, and reconnaissance 
assaults. TON-IoT is a great tool for protecting vital infrastructure, healthcare facilities, and smart cities because 
it combines network telemetry with data from the industrial IoT. These datasets are valuable, but they have a class 
imbalance that makes it hard to generalize models since normal traffic is so prevalent. This is why DNNs-BCT 
use stratified sampling, anomaly-based augmentation, and the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique 
(SMOTE) to improve learning. The model’s capacity to react to new cyber threats is further enhanced by adding 
real-world IoT traffic records from smart home and industrial IoT contexts.
To better understand the relative performance of the framework, current assessments may depend on 
restricted baseline comparisons. All three types of intrusion detection systems (IDS) traditional machine 
learning (e.g., Random Forest, SVM, and KNN), DL (e.g., CNN, LSTM, and Transformer-based models), and 
security frameworks that use blockchain technology should be evaluated against the suggested model for a 
more thorough evaluation. The system’s practical relevance and generalizability might be further enhanced by 
evaluations utilizing real-world IDS datasets such as CICIDS2017, NSL-KDD, or UNSW-NB15.
The suggested DNN-Blockchain architecture surpasses traditional rule-based intrusion detection systems 
(Fig. 6) with an astounding threat detection accuracy of 99.18%. This excellent accuracy of the DNN is driven 
by its ability to continuously learn from IoT traffic patterns and detect even the smallest changes connected 
with cyber threats. Using adaptive learning and multi-layer feature extraction, the model effectively identifies 
dangerous activities, including malware injections and DDoS attacks, ensuring powerful and consistent anomaly 
detection in IoT systems.
